---
title: "What cutoff marks a given percentage of a normal distribution?"
---

## What the question asks

What cutoff marks a given percentage of a normal distribution?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Convert the percentage to a probability between 0 and 1.

2. Identify mean and positive sd.

3. Run qnorm(probability,mean,sd).

## Runnable example

```{r}
cutoff <- qnorm(0.9,mean=100,sd=15)
print(cutoff)
print(pnorm(cutoff,100,15))
```

## Interpret the result

The modeled 90th-percentile cutoff is about 119.22. By construction, the normal CDF at that value is 0.9.

## Check before using your own data

Use a probability between 0 and 1, not 90 to represent a 90th-percentile cutoff.
